info.title: Micropod API · ContainerService
info.description:
## micropod.v1.ContainerService

Container lifecycle, logs, stats, and exec against the Apple `container`
 runtime.

post.description: Create a container without starting it (docker create).
Remove a container. Running containers require force.
Run a command inside a running container and return its output.

Inspect one container by ID. Fails with `not_found` when no container
 has that ID. `exit_code` is populated from the exit-code registry when
 the native backend recorded the container's exit.
Point-in-time resource usage for all running containers.
Stop a running container (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace period).

Block until the container exits or `timeout_seconds` elapses. Polls the
 exit-code registry and runtime state server-side (no blocking runtime
 wait); returns immediately when the container is already stopped.
 Fails with `not_found` when no container has that ID.

connect-protocol-version.title: Connect-Protocol-Version
connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is no limit on the number of messages.

type.description: A URL that acts as a globally unique identifier for the type of the serialized message. For example: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo`. This is used to determine the schema of the data in the `value` field and is the discriminator for the `debug` field.

value.description: The Protobuf message, serialized as bytes and base64-encoded. The specific message type is identified by the `type` field.

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Deserialized error detail payload. The 'type' field indicates the schema. This field is for easier debugging and should not be relied upon for application logic.

connect.error_details.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message, with an additional debug field for ConnectRPC error details.

id.title: id
id.description: The container ID; `container` uses the user-assigned name as the ID.

image.title: image
image.description: Image reference the container was created from.

state.title: state
state.description: Lifecycle state: running, stopped, exited, created, ...

networks.title: networks
networks.description: Names of networks the container is attached to.

ipv4Address.title: ipv4_address
ipv4Address.description: Resolved IPv4 address on the container network, if running.

rosetta.title: rosetta
rosetta.description: Runs x86_64 binaries via Rosetta translation.

useInit.title: use_init
useInit.description: An init process runs as PID 1 inside the container.

ssh.title: ssh
ssh.description: SSH access is enabled for the container.

virtualization.title: virtualization
virtualization.description: Uses full virtualization rather than the container runtime path.

runtimeHandler.title: runtime_handler
runtimeHandler.description: OCI runtime handler in use, if any.

exitCode.title: exit_code
exitCode.description: Exit code once the container has stopped.

runtime.title: runtime
runtime.description:
Execution engine that owns this container: "apple", "docker" or
 "sandbox" (see SystemService.ListRuntimes). Id-based calls are routed
 to this engine.

micropod.v1.Container.title: Container
micropod.v1.Container.description: Curated view of a container, mapped from `container list --format json`.

id.title: id
id.description: Container ID — `container` uses the user-assigned name as the ID.

micropod.v1.ContainerRef.title: ContainerRef
micropod.v1.ContainerRef.description: Reference to an existing container (or the ID returned by run/create).

cpuPercent.title: cpu_percent
cpuPercent.description: CPU usage as a percentage of one core.

networkRxBytes.title: network_rx_bytes
networkRxBytes.description: Bytes received over the container network.

networkTxBytes.title: network_tx_bytes
networkTxBytes.description: Bytes transmitted over the container network.

blockReadBytes.title: block_read_bytes
blockReadBytes.description: Bytes read from the block device.

blockWriteBytes.title: block_write_bytes
blockWriteBytes.description: Bytes written to the block device.

pids.title: pids
pids.description: Number of processes inside the container.

micropod.v1.ContainerStats.title: ContainerStats
micropod.v1.ContainerStats.description: Per-container resource counters within a StatsSnapshot.

force.title: force
force.description: Remove even if the container is still running.

micropod.v1.Empty.title: Empty
micropod.v1.Empty.description:
The Micropod daemon API is grouped into per-domain services, one per file:

   container.proto — ContainerService (lifecycle, logs, stats, exec)
   image.proto     — ImageService (list, pull, delete)
   volume.proto    — VolumeService (volumes + mount policy)
   network.proto   — NetworkService
   compose.proto   — Compose (up/down over a compose spec)
   system.proto    — SystemService (snapshot, usage, app updates)

 Empty is shared by every service, so it lives here.

id.title: id
id.description: Container ID (or name) to exec into.

command.title: command
command.description:
Command line to run inside the container, split on whitespace. Used only
 when `arguments` is empty; one of the two must be set (handlers reject
 an empty request with `invalid_argument`).

env.title: env
env.description: Extra environment variables as KEY=value pairs.

arguments.title: arguments
arguments.description:
Verbatim argv to run inside the container. Takes precedence over
 `command` when non-empty; elements are passed through unsplit.

output.title: output
output.description: Combined stdout (and stderr when not separable) of the command.

exitCode.title: exit_code
exitCode.description:
Guest process exit code. 0 on success; when the native runtime backend
 is active this is the real exit status rather than a CLI approximation.

error.title: error
error.description: Guest stderr, when the backend can separate the streams.

ids.title: ids
ids.description:
Restrict the snapshot to these container IDs. Empty means every running
 container. The native backend samples only the requested IDs.

snapshot.title: snapshot
snapshot.description: One stats snapshot covering every running container.

text.title: text
text.description: A single line of container output.

micropod.v1.Mount.title: Mount
micropod.v1.Mount.description: A volume or bind mount inside the container.

hostIp.title: host_ip
hostIp.description: Host interface IP to bind (empty = all interfaces).

micropod.v1.PortMapping.title: PortMapping
micropod.v1.PortMapping.description: A published port mapping between host and container.

image.title: image
image.description: Image reference to run, e.g. "alpine:3.20". Pulled if not present locally.

name.title: name
name.description: Optional container name; becomes the container ID.

cpus.title: cpus
cpus.description: CPU limit in cores, e.g. 0.5 for half a core.

labels.title: labels
labels.description: Arbitrary metadata labels on the container.

init.title: init
init.description: Run an init process as PID 1 to reap zombies.

arguments.title: arguments
arguments.description: Command + args override (image entrypoint is used when empty).

entrypoint.title: entrypoint
entrypoint.description: Entrypoint override (docker run --entrypoint); `arguments` become its args.

platform.title: platform
platform.description: Platform to select from a multi-arch image, e.g. "linux/arm64".

workdir.title: workdir
workdir.description: Working directory inside the container (docker run --workdir).

user.title: user
user.description: User (and optional group) to run as, e.g. "1000:1000" (docker run --user).

noPull.title: no_pull
noPull.description:
Fail with `not_found` instead of pulling when the image is absent
 locally (for the requested `platform`, when set). Lets callers own the
 pull and bound its duration.

capAdd.title: cap_add
capAdd.description:
Linux capabilities to add to the container's default set (docker run
 --cap-add). Names are case-insensitive, with or without the `CAP_`
 prefix ("NET_ADMIN" == "cap_net_admin"); "ALL" grants every capability.
 Unknown names fail with `invalid_argument`. The server normalises names
 to the `CAP_*` spelling before handing them to the runtime.

capDrop.title: cap_drop
capDrop.description:
Linux capabilities to remove from the container's set (docker run
 --cap-drop). Same spelling rules as `cap_add`; "ALL" drops every
 capability, so `cap_add` can then grant back a minimal set. Drops always
 win over an "ALL" grant — `cap_add: ["ALL"]` or `privileged` — so
 `privileged` + `cap_drop: ["SYS_MODULE"]` runs with every capability but
 SYS_MODULE. "ALL" here together with `privileged` or `cap_add: ["ALL"]`
 is contradictory and fails with `invalid_argument`.

rosetta.title: rosetta
rosetta.description:
Run x86_64 (linux/amd64) binaries through Rosetta translation (container
 run --rosetta). `true` forces Rosetta on. Unset or `false` keeps the
 server default: the native backend turns Rosetta on by itself when the
 selected image variant is amd64 on an Apple silicon host. Rosetta does
 not select an image variant — pair it with `platform: "linux/amd64"` to
 run the amd64 variant of a multi-arch image.

privileged.title: privileged
privileged.description:
Run the workload with the privileges a nested container engine
 (dockerd, containerd, buildkitd) needs — the micro-VM analogue of
 docker run --privileged: every Linux capability (as `cap_add: ["ALL"]`)
 and none of the runtime's default read-only or masked paths, so
 /proc/sys (IP forwarding, sysctls) and /sys/fs/cgroup are writable and
 /proc is not masked. The isolation boundary stays the micro-VM: host
 devices are not passed through. Named `cap_drop` entries still remove
 their capabilities; `cap_drop: ["ALL"]` with `privileged` fails with
 `invalid_argument`.

runtime.title: runtime
runtime.description:
Execution engine to run on: "apple" (a micro-VM per container via the
 Apple container runtime), "docker" (a Docker Engine socket) or
 "sandbox" (an ephemeral in-process micro-VM booted from a cached
 rootfs clone). Unset uses the server default (SetDefaultRuntime). An
 unknown or unavailable engine fails with `failed_precondition`.

sandbox.title: sandbox

micropod.v1.RunContainerRequest.title: RunContainerRequest
micropod.v1.RunContainerRequest.description: Shared request shape for run + create (docker run / docker create).

exposeHost.title: expose_host
exposeHost.description:
Host loopback ports the guest reaches as host.micropod.internal:<port>
 (e.g. a database on the host). Nothing else on the host is reachable.

allowHosts.title: allow_hosts
allowHosts.description:
Egress allowlist. When set, the VM has no route out of its own: all
 traffic leaves through a host proxy that refuses every other host.
 "*.example.com" matches subdomains only. Needs a network.

secrets.title: secrets
secrets.description:
Secrets by the environment variable name the guest sees. The guest gets
 a random placeholder; the host proxy swaps in the real value only in the
 request line and headers of HTTPS requests to the secret's `hosts`, so
 the credential never enters the VM. Needs a network.

dnsResolvers.title: dns_resolvers
dnsResolvers.description: Guest nameservers (default: the network gateway). Needs a network.

diskSizeMib.title: disk_size_mib
diskSizeMib.description: Root disk size in MiB for image bases (0 = the default, 8192).

micropod.v1.SandboxOptions.title: SandboxOptions
micropod.v1.SandboxOptions.description:
What a sandbox may reach beyond its own VM, and the credentials it may use
 without seeing them.

value.title: value
value.description:
The real value. SDKs read `from` environment variables on the caller's
 side and send the value here. CR, LF and NUL are refused.

command.title: command
command.description:
Not accepted: the API doesn't run host commands (removed in v0.11 for
 that reason; requests that set it fail with `invalid_argument`).

hosts.title: hosts
hosts.description:
HTTPS hosts whose requests get the real value ("*.example.com" matches
 subdomains).

expiresAt.title: expires_at
expiresAt.description:
When `value` stops working (RFC 3339). After it, requests to `hosts` fail
 closed (502) until UpdateSandboxSecret supplies a new value. Empty: the
 value doesn't expire.

micropod.v1.SandboxSecret.title: SandboxSecret
micropod.v1.SandboxSecret.description:
One secret: its current value and the hosts that may receive it. The API
 never runs programs on the host: to use a minted, expiring credential
 (`gcloud auth print-access-token`, a GitHub App token), mint it on the
 caller's side — the SDKs do this for `command` secrets — and push each
 new value with SandboxService.UpdateSandboxSecret.

containers.title: containers
containers.description: Per-container stats, one entry per running container.

sampledAt.title: sampled_at
sampledAt.description: ISO8601 timestamp the snapshot was taken.

micropod.v1.StatsSnapshot.title: StatsSnapshot
micropod.v1.StatsSnapshot.description:
Single snapshot of runtime resource usage for all running containers,
 mapped from `container stats --no-stream --format json`.

id.title: id
id.description: Container ID (or name) to stream logs from.

tail.title: tail
tail.description: Number of lines to replay from the end of the log before following.

boot.title: boot
boot.description: Include the vminitd guest boot log.

skipLines.title: skip_lines
skipLines.description:
Number of lines to drop from the start of the stream (after `tail` is
 applied). Lets a client re-open a stream after a transport error
 without replaying lines it already delivered.

id.title: id
id.description: Container ID (or name) to wait on.

timeoutSeconds.title: timeout_seconds
timeoutSeconds.description:
Seconds to wait for the container to exit. 0 selects the server default
 (30); values above 300 are capped at 300.

exited.title: exited
exited.description: True when the container is no longer running or stopping.

known.title: known
known.description:
True when `exit_code` is authoritative (recorded by the exit-code
 registry). False for containers the server did not start itself or
 whose entry aged out.

exitCode.title: exit_code
exitCode.description: Process exit code; only meaningful when `known` is true.

state.title: state
state.description:
Runtime state observed at return: running, stopping, stopped, created
 or unknown.
